answer: An applicant locks 320 spendable POA in a 40-hour haven escrow, then publishes a commit-reveal seed. Every 90 minutes it must release the next pulse in a hash spiral of 20 one-time HKDF signatures; missing a pulse or reusing a key slashes the escrow to zero. A public mirror of the seed commitment and the pulse log lets any peer recompute the chain and apply the slash without a trusted operator. A farm of N aliases therefore immobilizes 320N coins and must babysit N independent clocks; one missed beat erases the stake, so cloning has a negative expected value.
